Sorry, that's a frustrating way to lose two hours. I've saved it to the project's EngramDB memory as a high-priority warning, so future sessions will flag `PAYMENTS_LIVE` early when payments act strangely.

The string `PAYMENTS_LIVE` doesn't appear anywhere in this repo. The only payment code is `tests/test_payments.py`, which posts straight to `https://sandbox.payments.example`. So the switch is probably in a dependency, deployment config, or a separate service. I noted that in the memory too.

If you can tell me where it lives, I can make the fallback visible so this doesn't happen again. Options include:
- logging a loud warning at startup when the fake gateway is active
- failing on startup outside dev/test unless the fake gateway is explicitly enabled
- documenting the variable in the README and `.env.example`
